title: Linux.Mirai_Trojan_Investigation_a6a
description: Investigate a compromised Linux host infected with the Mirai trojan.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The victim host in your network has exhibited unusual behavior, including unexpected network connections and system resource consumption. Your task is to investigate and determine the nature of the compromise.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- IP Address: 192.168.60.10
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- IP Address: 192.168.60.10
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Services
levels.content: Investigate the system for unauthorized or suspicious services running on the compromised host. Enumerate running services and distinguish legitimate services from trojan-related services. Look specifically for the network-diagnostics.timer service which is known to be associated with the Mirai trojan.
levels.solution: Check the status of all services and look for any that appear unusual or out of place. Use commands like `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services and `systemctl status <service_name>` to check the status of specific services. Pay special attention to the network-diagnostics.timer service.

hints.title: Check for Unusual Services
hints.content: Check the status of all services and look for any that appear unusual or out of place.

hints.title: Look for Specific Timer
hints.content: Use commands like `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services and `systemctl status <service_name>` to check the status of specific services. Pay special attention to the network-diagnostics.timer service.

hints.title: Identify Malicious Service
hints.content: Look for services that are not part of the standard system installation or those that have unusual names, specifically the network-diagnostics.timer service.

levels.title: Identify Scheduled Task or Timer
levels.content: Determine whether a scheduled task or timer is responsible for automatically executing the malware. Identify scheduled execution persistence mechanisms (e.g., cron, systemd timers, Windows Scheduled Tasks). Specifically, look for the network-diagnostics.timer which is known to be associated with the Mirai trojan.
levels.solution: Examine the systemd timers and services to find any that might be related to the suspicious activity. Use commands like `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers and `systemctl status <timer_name>` to check the status of specific timers. Pay special attention to the network-diagnostics.timer.

hints.title: Examine Systemd Timers
hints.content: Examine the systemd timers and services to find any that might be related to the suspicious activity.

hints.title: Look for Specific Timer
hints.content: Use commands like `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers and `systemctl status <timer_name>` to check the status of specific timers. Pay special attention to the network-diagnostics.timer.

hints.title: Identify Malicious Timer
hints.content: Look for timers that are not part of the standard system installation or those that have unusual names, specifically the network-diagnostics.timer.

levels.title: Locate Malware Files
levels.content: Locate files installed by the malware on the compromised host. Correlate suspicious activity with files introduced by the trojan. Specifically, look for the /var/lib/.netd/install.log file which is known to be associated with the Mirai trojan.
levels.solution: Search for hidden directories and files that might contain malware components or collected data. Use commands like `find / -type d -name '.*' 2>/dev/null` to find hidden directories and `find / -type f -name '.*' 2>/dev/null` to find hidden files. Pay special attention to the /var/lib/.netd/install.log file.

hints.title: Search for Hidden Files
hints.content: Search for hidden directories and files that might contain malware components or collected data.

hints.title: Look for Specific File
hints.content: Use commands like `find / -type d -name '.*' 2>/dev/null` to find hidden directories and `find / -type f -name '.*' 2>/dev/null` to find hidden files. Pay special attention to the /var/lib/.netd/install.log file.

hints.title: Identify Malicious File
hints.content: Look for files in unusual locations or those that have unusual names, specifically the /var/lib/.netd/install.log file.
